19.0.0.en: "Alleluia": an expression meaning joy and rejoicing, and it also carries praise and glorification.

19.0.1.en: A great multitude: an expression of the large number, and also the variety of groups.

19.0.2.en: After that St. John heard a voice coming from all the heavenly creation (angels and the spirits of the martyrs and saints) declaring their joy, and they rejoiced with thanksgiving, praising God, and the words of their praise carried and made clear the reasons for this joy.

19.0.3.en: The first reason is the greatness of the Lord the Savior and the greatness of His salvation, for He alone is the owner of glory and honor and is almighty, and this is what the Church repeats in the prayers of the Pascha Week when she prays: "Yours is the power, the glory, the blessing and the majesty forever."

19.1.0.en: The second reason is the joy that God's judgments are just judgments, and even if He delays in them, the condemnation of evil gladdens everyone who lived and strove in righteousness and godliness, especially when they see the condemnation of the kingdom of evil and its head, Satan, and their being tormented just as they also tormented His holy children. And just as the bliss that the faithful children of God will enjoy is eternal, so also the torment of the kingdom of evil will be eternal, for the smoke of her burning rises up forever and ever.

19.2.0.en: After St. John gathered all the heavenly creation in the scene of praise and rejoicing, he draws closer to the throne of God, where the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures surrounding the throne of God (see ch. 4:4-8) repeat the scene of worship and cry out like the cry of the heavenly multitude, "Amen; Alleluia," confirming their sharing with the multitude in joy and praise.

19.3.0.en: Came out of the throne: we do not know whose this voice is, but it came out from the center of heaven, that is, the throne of God.

19.3.1.en: Ye that fear him: those who lived in the fear of God, and this fear kept them from the kingdom of evil. Both small and great: that is, whatever the stature or rank, the call to praise is general for everyone. A call came from one of the heavenly creatures declaring that everyone must share in praise, singing and gladness and in confessing the work of God and His justice.

19.4.0.en: The whole heavenly creation responded to the call by offering praise and glory to God, and because of the intensity and greatness of its voice it is described as "the voice of a great multitude," like the sound of the falling waters of mighty waterfalls and like the sound of thunder terrifying in people's ears. As for the subject and words of its praise, it was the proclamation of the complete Kingdom of God and His absolute sovereignty over everything after the end and passing away of the kingdom of evil, and in this they present to us a third reason for the song of joy.

19.5.0.en: The marriage of the Lamb: the proclamation of the Kingdom of God at His Second Coming.

19.5.1.en: His wife: His striving Church, for whom the time of her joy and the proclamation of her victory has come.

19.5.2.en: A fourth reason for the joys of heaven, which is the proclamation of the beginning of the joys of the marriage of the Lamb, when He comes in His Second Coming and announces the end of life on earth and the beginning of eternal life and happiness. The phrase "the marriage of the Lamb" means that it is a joy whose center and source is Christ Himself, while His wife is a symbol of the faithful, striving Church that endured terrors and whose time of delight has at last come... The meaning also includes Christ's eternal union (expressed by marriage) with each individual human soul that kept its purity and was not defiled by the world and never made Babylon its home, and for this its reward is to put on the dress of the bride and appear in her most splendid adornment.

19.6.0.en: Her adornment and purity is expressed by the pure linen (fine linen), which points to her purity, cleanness and righteousness (the Church or the soul), for it is known that nothing unclean will enter heaven (Rev 21:8), and the expression "was granted" means that Christ in His justice and vengeance on Satan and his kingdom and followers also rewards those of His holy children who were faithful, since He alone is the source of every gift, joy, grace and eternal happiness.

19.6.1.en: My Lord and beloved God, meditation and gazing on this beautiful and wonderful scene creates in the soul longings and eagerness that make it understand the feelings of St. Paul when he declared the desire of his heart and his wish to depart from earth to heaven, where the marriage of the Lamb is. But these longings, my Lord, often wither in the heart and I forget them.. So I beg You, my Lord, do not allow the world and all its concerns to take these feelings from my heart, but always renew my longing for You and for the splendor of the glory of Your heavenly wedding... that no one may take my crown.

19.7.s.en: (2) The blessedness and happiness of the saints

19.7.0.en: The angel commanded St. John to write, a command that has been repeated many times, and the purpose of repeating the command is to highlight the importance of what is coming. What God wanted written and to reach us is a message of encouragement to urge us to continue the spiritual striving to the end. First he declares the happiness of the faithful strivers who have been given (the invitation) to enter the glories of the Kingdom, and second he affirms that this will happen and is certain, for the words and promises of God are true and sure.

19.8.0.en: Before the awe of the situation and the joy of the good news he had heard, St. John found himself prostrating in humility before the angel, who forbade him, since he (the angel) is also one of God's creatures and servants, and worship should be to God alone.

19.8.1.en: That have the testimony of Jesus: an expression that refers to the earthly creation and its duty of witness, preaching and praise to the Lord Jesus.

19.8.2.en: The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy: that is, witness and preaching in the name of the Lord Christ is the foundation of all prophecy, for the aim of the prophecies of the prophets in the Old Testament was the coming Christ, and in the New Testament the word prophecy means more teaching, because it speaks of the coming Kingdom of God, and every teaching in the New Testament has Christ as its aim.

19.8.3.en: A note: "worship God": some exploit this verse and attack the tradition of the Coptic people of bowing before the Father bishops and kissing their hands..; but the firm and most beautiful teaching in the Church is that the submission and bowing is not to the person of the man himself (for we do not worship anyone but God) but we believe that we bow to the grace and gift of the priesthood (the priesthood of Christ Himself), which was handed over through Christ to the Apostles, and from them to the Father bishops by the holy breathing (Jn 20:22). The meaning, simply, is that we worship Christ who is hidden in the glory of His priesthood. In addition, all people agree that bowing is respect for those of standing in all the world.

19.8.4.en: I wish, my brother, that you would remember the Kingdom with all its joys, so that you leave behind the passing pleasures of sin and also make light of the temporary pains of life, and strive diligently with fervent worship and the labors of service by which you express your love for God and for all around you.

19.9.s.en: (3) The scene of the triumphant Christ

19.9.0.en: St. John describes a new scene for us, as he sees the Lord Christ sitting on a white horse, the same sight he saw at the opening of the first seal (ch. 6:2), and this vision makes clear to us some of the attributes of the Lord Christ:

19.9.1.en: a) Power: for He is a warrior horseman who went out to conquer (ch. 6). b) Purity and cleanness: for the color white is always a symbol of purity and cleanness.

19.9.2.en: c) Faithful and True: faithful in completing His redemption and proclaiming His victory, and true in His promises and covenants to His children and those who love Him.

19.9.3.en: d) Just: for He judges in justice and gives each one according to his work.

19.9.4.en: e) Supporting: for He fights with His children and for them against all the schemes of the evil enemy.

19.10.0.en: His eyes were as a flame of fire: that is, the Searcher of hidden things; see also (ch. 1:14, ch. 2:18). On his head were many crowns: every king and kingdom has one crown, but the many crowns are a figure for His absolute authority over all creation and the nations, for He is King of kings.

19.10.1.en: He had a name written, that no man knew: because His name is the essence of God Himself, unlimited and incomprehensible to man.

19.10.2.en: St. John continues the description of the Lord Christ, declaring to us the power of His eyes, from which nothing hides or is hidden, and the authority of His absolute kingship over all, and also pointing to His wonderful and glorious name, whose dimensions no one grasps, and this reminds us of Moses' meeting with God (Ex 3:13, 14) when he asked about His name and God answered him "I AM THAT I AM," that is, the One who is and who will be, and there is no single name that expresses His divine essence (see also Isa 9:6), where Isaiah prophesied about the birth of Christ and described His name as wonderful.

19.11.0.en: Clothed with a vesture: wearing a garment like the garments of the priests; see the explanation of (ch. 1:13). The scene that St. John sees here is very similar to what he saw at the beginning of the Book of Revelation (ch. 1), but he adds to it that the garment of His priesthood is dipped in blood, and the meaning here is very clear, for he sees the Lord Christ the High Priest (Heb 4:14) and sees Him also as a sacrifice of redemption offered for us all, so He is the sacrifice and He is also the priest who offered it.

19.11.1.en: His name is The Word of God: and it is the divine name of the Lord Christ or His hypostatic name (Jn 1:1). This was explained in detail in the commentary on the Gospel of John.

19.12.0.en: The armies: the name of armies or heavenly hosts has been associated with the angels, but there is nothing here to prevent the multitudes of the saints from being with them also.

19.12.2.en: As the Lord Christ went out on a white horse, He also gave by His grace to all who completed their striving and overcame to go out and follow Him in the procession of His victory, riding white horses like Him, as if He makes them partners with Him in the glories of His victory, and He clothed them in white linen, a symbol of the purity of their conduct and their cleanness by which and for which they lived.

19.13.0.en: A sharp sword: that is, His word or His speech; see (ch. 1:16). With it he should smite the nations: a figure for the severity of His word by which He will judge the nations.

19.13.1.en: A rod of iron: that is, His strong authority over His enemies; see also (ch. 12:5). The winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God: an expression used to highlight the power of God's vengeance on evil and the wicked and His unlimited ability; see also (ch. 14:20). St. John continues describing the scene of his vision of Christ, making clear to us the power of His word, which will judge the wicked since they did not act on it and did not turn back from their evil, so His word becomes a judgment on them, as the Lord Christ Himself said, "the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day" (Jn 12:48), and likewise He will have the authority of a king over them (the rod) since the time of their repayment has come. And to highlight the intensity of the wrath and vengeance, St. John goes on and reminds us of the scene of "the winepress," for the Romans used to make stone basins dug in the ground and put grapes in them, and some slaves would go down barefoot to tread the grapes with their feet to press them as a first step in preparing wine, so likewise the enemies of God become like trodden grapes.

19.14.0.en: In (v. 12) St. John mentioned that the name of God is great and no one knows its dimensions, but here he mentions that God, that is, the Lord Christ, is clothed with His name "on his vesture," and the meaning is that the greatness of the name of God covers the whole world. As for the name being written on the thigh, this is a reference to the power and the continuous divine work in saving His children and refuting evil; and the name declared to us here, "King of kings and Lord of lords," makes clear to us that the glory of God and His Kingdom has no likeness in any of the great kingdoms of the world that people have known, indeed in truth there is not the slightest comparison, for Christ alone is the Lord of all creation and its King, whether this creation is heavenly or earthly.

19.14.1.en: The words can also be interpreted symbolically, considering that His garment signifies His Church, which proclaims His name before the whole world for repentance and the acceptance of salvation.

19.14.2.en: Let us ask ourselves every day before we sleep .. was Christ truly my King and my Lord all day long .. or did I, without meaning to, have another king and lord from the material things of the world .. My God, I want You alone to be my only King, but I often go astray, so I beg You, my God, help me to consecrate my whole heart to You alone and desire nothing but Your Kingdom.

19.15.s.en: (4) The scene of the end of evil

19.15.0.en: St. John continues his vision of the scene of the last victory, declaring the appearance of an angel standing in the sun, that is, visible to all, and he cried with a loud voice because of the importance of what he would proclaim to all. He called to all the fowls of heaven, meaning the birds of prey that eat flesh, for God has prepared for them a great supper from the remains of the members of the kingdom of evil who were trodden down (v. 15), for these birds to eat them.. and he mentioned in the explanation of (v. 18) these members, for they were the kings of evil, its commanders, its mighty men and its horsemen, and the birds ate their flesh, from the greatest of them to the smallest, and the scene as a whole is a completion of the picture of God's wrath and vengeance on the wicked.

19.15.1.en: A note: many of the Fathers reflected on the difference between the scene of the "marriage supper" (v. 9), which is for those who love the holy name of God, that joyful supper, and this supper, great in its ruin and calamity for the wicked.

19.16.0.en: In a last scene representing the last desperate attempt made by the beast, the representative of Satan and his fiercest commander (ch. 13:1), as he gathers all his wicked followers to make a final war against Christ after the proclamation of their judgment and destruction, the final end comes and the Lord Christ seizes the beast and his representative the Antichrist, who led the nations astray by the wonders he performed (see ch. 13:11-17) until they went whoring after him and left God.

19.16.1.en: Them that had received the mark of the beast: that is, those who followed Satan and accepted him as their god instead of God (see ch. 13:15, ch. 14:11). Both were cast: that is, the beast and the false prophet.

19.16.2.en: Alive: a figure for the severity of the torment, for how cruel it is for something living to be burned.

19.16.3.en: A lake of fire burning with brimstone: a figure for the breadth of the circle of the fire, "lake," and its intensity, "brimstone," and it will be mentioned also in (ch. 20, 21), and it is a reference to eternal judgment and endless torment, and it is not hell, that is, the temporary place where the wicked await judgment.

19.16.4.en: A note: if the name of the beast is mentioned alone, it is a symbolic indication of the kingdom of Satan and his mark, and if the name of the dragon is mentioned with it, the dragon is the great Satan and the beast is his greatest commander, and with them the false prophet (ch. 13:2, ch. 16:13).

19.17.0.en: The remnant: that is, the earthly kings and leaders of evil other than the beast and the Antichrist, whose judgment was completed.

19.17.1.en: Slain with the sword of him that sat: that is, their judgment was carried out by the judgments of His word.

19.17.2.en: All the fowls were filled: a figure for the end of evil and the completion of God's just judgment.

19.17.3.en: In reference to the scene of judgment, all the wicked will stand before God and be tried and condemned before His word and His commandment that they neglected and squandered, so it will be like the sword that first bears witness to their transgression and then leads them to destruction, so that they become a meal for the birds of prey of heaven, in a painful and terrifying scene and a certain fate for everyone who neglected God's successive warnings (v. 17).

19.17.4.en: Do not persist in your sin like Satan and all his wicked followers, who await eternal torment. You are different from him because you are a child of God, and however great your fall may be, return to Him quickly and He will embrace you and forgive you and support you with His power and adorn you with His virtues. Remembering the judgment keeps you away from many desires and from negligence and laziness, and you win the salvation of your soul.

19.17.5.en: The binding of Satan, his loosing, and the thousand-year reign: introduction to the chapter: this chapter is considered one of the very important parts of the Book of Revelation, since it deals with the subject of "the reign of Christ for a thousand years.." which has led some to actually await the Second Coming of Christ to reign on earth. Of course the Church rejects this direction in interpretation; for the book as a whole is a spiritual book and all its meanings are symbolic, and many, indeed all, of the numbers and figures that come in it have no relation to earthly time in its days and hours by which we work now.
